newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco's copper production rises in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Codelco's copper production rises in 1996.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco said its fine copper output rose to 1.22 million tonnes last year, up 55,000 tonnes on 1995.
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, reported pre-tax profits of $1.1 billion in 1996.

The earnings were "despite a sharp fall in copper prices and the slide to less than half in the price of molybdenum," said president Marcos Lima in a public address on the firm's performance last year.
Codelco continued to cut production costs last year with cathode costs at $0.72 a pound and direct costs at close to $0.49, said Lima.
"The accumulated reduction since 1993 is 10.8 cents a pound (for cathodes) and 12.4 cents a pound (cash costs) for both indicators," said Lima.
Codelco expects costs to fall by a more modest 0.5-1 cent a pound this year as no new mines or extensions of existing pits will come into operation in this period which would reduce costs, he said.
"Every year it is more difficult to continue lowering costs without incorporating operations with lower costs, like Radomiro Tomic," said Lima.
He was referring Codelco's new oxides mine which will produce 150,000 tonnes of cathodes a year when it comes on line next year.
The corporation's objective is to be among the lowest quarter of world copper producers in terms of costs, he said.
"This is the obly way of guaranteeing our competitiveness," said Lima.
